key_insight: In this Alzheimer’s MRI study—not cancer drug discovery—strong PVS segmentation accuracy did not guarantee preservation of biologically relevant associations.
clinical_relevance: Automated PVS measurements require cohort-specific validation before supporting Alzheimer’s biomarker research or clinical inference.
method: Benchmarked five open-source nnU-Net-based PVS segmentation models against manual labels.
Evaluated performance across brain regions, diagnoses, scanners, PVS severity, and white matter hyperintensity burden.
Tested whether model-derived PVS burden reproduced manual-label associations with Alzheimer’s biomarkers.
evidence_signal: Across 60 ADNI-3 participants and 12 external VALDO scans, ADNI-PVS-Net achieved internal Dice of 0.58 ± 0.14 but external Dice ≤0.11; only AD-trained models reproduced the expected PVS–amyloid relationship.
watch_item: Domain shifts and white matter hyperintensity misclassification can distort PVS burden and downstream biomarker associations, even when Dice scores appear competitive.
paper_title: Examining the Clinical Utility of Deep Learning Models for Perivascular Space Segmentation in Alzheimer's Disease
